- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add 3–5% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth 3–5 day moving average before forecasting to reduce overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a sharp spike, model often fails to correct; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the period when sentiment is positive; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 14-day high if sentiment >0.5.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day prices for calibration.
